report.summary: Chunk 9 of daedalus/spine/picker.py: defines load_map_state, map_state_trustworthy, helper functions, and docref_candidates; includes extensive docstrings with claims about behavior and history.
risks: map_state_trustworthy | medium | Docstring claims digest_ok from daedalus.mapping.drift is used, but the import is inside the function; if daedalus.mapping.drift is unavailable, the function returns untrusted. This is intentional but may surprise callers expecting a different behavior. | Check if the import error handling is documented and consistent with the module's design.

map_state_trustworthy | medium | Docstring claims 'a snapshot that records no repo_state.head cannot answer the second question and is therefore NOT trusted', but the code delegates to _repo_state_freshness, which is not defined in this chunk. The claim is uncheckable. | Verify _repo_state_freshness implementation in another chunk.

docref_candidates | high | Docstring claims this function is 'THE ONE THAT CLOSES THE LOOP' and that it produces work inside the permitted tree, but the function signature returns a tuple of candidates and warnings; the actual behavior depends on the report argument and other modules. The claim is uncheckable from this chunk. | Review the full implementation and its integration with the loop.

MAP_STATE_REL_PATH | low | Constant defined as 'docs/architecture-state.json' but no validation that this path exists or is correct relative to repo_root. | Ensure the path is correct and that load_map_state handles missing file gracefully (it does).
todos: Review the implementation of _repo_state_freshness to verify freshness check logic.
Verify that docref_candidates actually produces candidates as claimed and that the loop can process them.
Ensure that the map_state_trustworthy function's fallback to untrusted when daedalus.mapping.drift is unavailable is acceptable.

claims.text: Read ``docs/architecture-state.json``, or ``{}`` if it cannot be read.
claims.why: The function opens the path and returns {} on OSError, ValueError, or UnicodeDecodeError.

claims.text: Same degrade-to-empty contract as :func:`load_inventory`: the picker's job is to rank work, not to be the thing that breaks when a generated file is mid-write.
claims.why: load_inventory is not defined in this chunk, so the claim about its contract cannot be verified.

claims.text: INTEGRITY -- has anyone hand-edited the generated file? ``daedalus.mapping.drift`` states the rule: *any verb that INHERITS lists from an existing snapshot rather than rescanning has to ask this first and refuse on a mismatch*. Ranking work out of those lists is exactly such a verb.
claims.why: The claim references daedalus.mapping.drift and its rules, which are not in this chunk.

claims.text: FRESHNESS -- does the snapshot describe the tree we are standing in? This question used to be missing, and its absence was justified in this very docstring with the sentence "a generated file's defence is its digest". That was wrong, and it cost something measurable.
claims.why: The claim refers to historical justification and consequences not present in the code.

claims.text: A digest proves nobody tampered with the file; it says NOTHING about which tree was scanned. A snapshot generated thirty commits ago verifies its digest perfectly.
claims.why: The claim is about digest properties, but the actual digest check is delegated to daedalus.mapping.drift.digest_ok, which is not in this chunk.

claims.text: What that bought: an agent executed the loop's top recommendation, which asserted ``daedalus/compaction.py`` was an unreachable island. On the live tree it was not an island at all -- it was ``unknown``, because of a string literal in a smoke-test prompt. The picker had SUPPRESSED the stale inventory (which has a freshness gate) while TRUSTING the stale map (which had none), and acted on a description of a tree that no longer existed.
claims.why: This is a historical anecdote; none of the mentioned events or files are verifiable from this chunk.

claims.text: So both questions are asked, and both must pass. A snapshot that records no ``repo_state.head`` cannot answer the second one and is therefore NOT trusted -- fail closed, the same rule the inventory follows. Until the generator stamps the revision it scanned, that is the honest verdict, and reporting "I have no trustworthy map" beats ranking work from a tree that is gone.
claims.why: The code calls _repo_state_freshness, which is not defined in this chunk; the claim about repo_state.head cannot be verified.

claims.text: Its ONLY importers are tests, so the behaviour is already pinned: wiring it up is cheap and a regression would be caught.
claims.why: The claim about importers depends on the architecture map, which is not in this chunk.

claims.text: NOTHING imports it at all -- not even a test. Whatever you decide, add a test that exercises the path you keep.
claims.why: Same as above: depends on external data.

claims.text: THE ONE THAT CLOSES THE LOOP. Every other source in this module produces source surgery under ``daedalus/``; the installed self-policy permits ``docs/``, ``tests/`` and ``README.md``. Measured 2026-07-29, the intersection was EMPTY -- the picker ranked seventeen candidates and a local writer was permitted to attempt none of them. This source produces work inside the permitted tree without widening the tree, which is the difference between closing the loop and lowering the fence to reach it.
claims.why: The claim references module-level behavior, self-policy, historical measurements, and other sources not present in this chunk.

observations.what: The docstring for map_state_trustworthy contains a lengthy narrative about a historical bug, but the code itself is straightforward: it checks digest and freshness.
The function docref_candidates has a docstring that makes grandiose claims about 'closing the loop', but the function signature is simple and its behavior depends entirely on the report argument.
The constant MAP_STATE_REL_PATH is defined but not used within this chunk; it is used by load_map_state.
The helper functions _map_island_instruction and _map_shim_instruction are not called within this chunk; they are likely used elsewhere.
